title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
synopsis: Logan walks away from a military unit after its commander orders an attack on civilians. Years later, grief draws him back to the man who gave that order.
verdictRationale: The villagers have nothing to offer Logan. Protecting them costs him both a livelihood and his brother’s company. That choice gives the film moral weight. Yet the pleasure of watching Logan settle scores often competes with the better use he finds for his strength in freeing prisoners.
ageRationale: Repeated impalements, a painful medical experiment and a childhood killing make this a demanding watch for younger teens.
reflection: In the village, Logan can do good only by breaking ranks. What would loyalty to Victor look like if it included trying to stop him from hurting someone?

title: X-Men: First Class
synopsis: Charles and Erik recruit young mutants during the Cold War. A shared enemy brings the friends together, but each wants a different future for the people they train.
verdictRationale: Charles asks Erik to protect people who may never welcome him. Erik’s childhood makes his anger understandable, and the choice to avenge his mother shows what that anger can cost. Their friendship invites real discernment, alongside sexualized scenes and a killing staged for a prolonged look.
ageRationale: A child witnesses his mother’s murder in a concentration camp. A later revenge killing unfolds in close detail. Lingerie, seduction and strong profanity add to the age recommendation.
reflection: Charles has heard Erik’s reasons for revenge. Speaking for peace costs him the agreement of a friend he loves. The beatitude gives families a way to consider what that friendship asks of him.

title: Dark Phoenix
synopsis: Jean Grey saves astronauts and returns to Earth carrying a force she struggles to control. The crisis exposes choices Charles made when she was in his care.
verdictRationale: The shuttle rescue shows the team at its best. Later, Raven asks who bears the risk when Charles seeks public favor. His eventual admission of wrongdoing gives parents a concrete way to discuss repentance, though the story spends more time on destructive confrontations than on rebuilding Jean’s trust.
ageRationale: A fatal accident, the violent death of a teammate, strong language and drinking in grief warrant particular care with younger teens, especially after a family loss.
reflection: Raven looks past the applause for a successful rescue and asks whose lives Charles risked. Her objection invites a Christian leader to hear correction even when everyone else is offering praise.

title: The New Mutants
synopsis: Dani survives a disaster and wakes in a locked facility for young mutants. When frightening memories begin taking physical form, the residents must decide whether to trust each other or their doctor.
verdictRationale: Dani’s father goes back for his neighbors, and Rahne stays with Dani in a moment of despair. Both show genuine care. The site’s rubric assigns its Destructive verdict to the prominence of Dani and Rahne’s romance. Families should also weigh the repeated use of abuse and trauma as horror imagery.
ageRationale: The sustained horror, a suicidal crisis, memories of abuse and a violent death carry more weight for age guidance than the superhero branding suggests.
reflection: Rahne cannot undo the loss of Dani’s family. She can stay, listen and help Dani reach safety. Bearing a burden sometimes begins with refusing to leave someone alone with it.
